chapter.name: Working with Fractions
chapter.blurb: Multiplying a fraction with a whole number and with another fraction, cancelling common factors, how the size of a product or quotient compares with the numbers used, division by reciprocals, and word problems.

scope: Multiply a whole number and a fraction as repeated addition (5 x 3 km, 3 x 1/4 km)
Multiply a fraction by a whole number by dividing by the denominator and multiplying by the numerator (1/5 x 3 = 3/5, 2/5 x 3 = 6/5)
Convert a mixed fraction to an improper fraction before multiplying, and convert products back to mixed fractions
Multiply two fractions using a unit square, and read the product as the shaded fraction of the whole (1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8, 3/4 x 2/5 = 3/10)
Connect the area of a rectangle with fractional sides to the product of the sides
Use the rows-and-columns picture to show 1/b x 1/d = 1/(b x d)
Use Brahmagupta's formula a/b x c/d = (a x c)/(b x d), writing a whole number with denominator 1
Cancel common factors of numerators and denominators before multiplying to reach the lowest form
Solve word problems that multiply fractions, including mixed fractions and fractions of a fraction
Compare a product with the numbers multiplied depending on whether they are greater than 1 or between 0 and 1
Use that the order of multiplication does not change a product of fractions
Rewrite a division as a missing-factor multiplication and use the reciprocal to divide by a fraction
Use Brahmagupta's formula a/b divided by c/d = a/b x d/c
Compare a quotient with the dividend and divisor depending on whether the divisor is greater than 1 or between 0 and 1
Solve word problems needing division by a fraction or a whole number, including the brick, fountain and cowrie-shell problems and the fractional-relations square problem
Adding and subtracting fractions as a topic of its own -- only used inside word problems, the methods were taught earlier
Decimals, percentages, ratio and proportion in fraction problems -- not part of this chapter
Multiplying or dividing negative fractions and rational numbers -- not covered here
A formal algebraic proof of the multiplication or division formula -- the chapter justifies them with pictures and the missing-factor idea
Division by zero and the reciprocal of zero -- not discussed in the chapter

concepts.name: Multiplying a whole number and a fraction
concepts.description: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number, or a whole number by a fraction, including mixed fractions and converting back to a mixed fraction.
concepts.idea: Multiplying a whole number by a fraction is repeated addition of that fraction; a fraction multiplier takes that part of the whole number.
concepts.rule: To find a/b x n, divide n by the denominator b and multiply the result by the numerator a; convert a mixed fraction to an improper fraction first.

concepts.name: Multiplying two fractions with a unit square
concepts.description: Finding the product of two fractions by shading a unit square, and linking it to the area of a rectangle with fractional sides.
concepts.idea: On a unit square one fraction sets the columns and the other the rows, and the product is the shaded part of the whole.
concepts.rule: The whole is cut into (denominator of one) x (denominator of the other) equal parts; 1/b x 1/d = 1/(b x d); the area of a rectangle with fractional sides equals the product of its sides.
concepts.example: 1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8 because the whole square has 2 columns and 4 rows, so 8 equal parts of which 1 is shaded.

concepts.name: Brahmagupta's multiplication rule and cancelling
concepts.description: Multiplying fractions by multiplying numerators and denominators, cancelling common factors first, and giving the product in lowest form.
concepts.idea: A fraction stays the same when its numerator and denominator are divided by the same factor, so common factors can be cancelled across a product.
concepts.rule: a/b x c/d = (a x c)/(b x d); a whole number n is n/1; cancel common factors of any numerator with any denominator before multiplying.

concepts.name: Size of a product and order of multiplication
concepts.description: Deciding whether a product is bigger or smaller than the numbers multiplied, and using that changing the order does not change the product.
concepts.idea: Multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes a number bigger, and by a number between 0 and 1 makes it smaller.
concepts.rule: If both numbers exceed 1 the product exceeds both; if both lie between 0 and 1 the product is less than both; if one exceeds 1 and one is below 1 the product lies between them; a/b x c/d = c/d x a/b.
concepts.example: 3/4 x 2/5 = 3/10, which is less than both 3/4 and 2/5.

concepts.name: Dividing fractions using reciprocals
concepts.description: Dividing by a whole number or fraction by multiplying with the reciprocal of the divisor.
concepts.idea: Dividing by a number is finding the missing factor, and the reciprocal is the number that multiplies the divisor to give 1.
concepts.rule: The reciprocal of a/b is b/a; a/b divided by c/d = a/b x d/c = (a x d)/(b x c).

concepts.name: Size of a quotient compared with dividend and divisor
concepts.description: Predicting whether a quotient will be greater or less than the dividend depending on the divisor.
concepts.idea: Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the result bigger, because more small pieces fit into the dividend.
concepts.rule: If the divisor is between 0 and 1 the quotient is greater than the dividend; if the divisor is greater than 1 the quotient is less than the dividend.
concepts.example: 6 divided by 1/4 = 24, which is greater than 6, because the divisor 1/4 is less than 1.

concepts.name: Word problems and fraction-of-a-fraction chains
concepts.description: Solving multi-step problems that multiply or divide fractions, including the brick, fountain, rate and cowrie-shell problems and chains of fractions of fractions.
concepts.idea: A situation is turned into one multiplication or division of fractions by asking which quantity is being scaled or shared.
concepts.rule: Total = number of items x size of one item; number of items = total divided by size of one item; "a fraction of" a quantity means multiply.
concepts.example: 15/2 sq units covered by bricks of area 1/25 needs 15/2 divided by 1/25 = 375/2 bricks.
